title: Model Ecosystem Friction Audit & Remediation Sprint
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Run a focused audit to map friction points customers and internal teams face when switching or integrating alternate open models (tokenization differences, API surface mismatches, quantization/precision regressions, latency/cost delta, licensing and provenance). Produce a prioritized remediation backlog and prototype compatibility shims to reduce enterprise procurement and integration cost of switching models. Deliverables: 1) friction map heatmap 2) remediation backlog with estimated effort and owner 3) two compatibility shim prototypes (tokenizer adapter + quant-profile recommendation engine) 4) integration test harness and regression dataset for model swap validation 5) executive one-pager for sales/CS.
background: Business context: increasing enterprise demand for fallback/supplier switching paths. PM research and sales calls show customers delay migrations due to non-obvious integration work (tokenization drift causing hallucinations, embedding dimension mismatches, or ops complexity for per-model quantization). This creates renewal and procurement risk and reduces our ability to arbitrate cost/latency trade-offs for customers. The audit will unify signals from field research, infra telemetry, and engineering test runs to produce actionable remediation work for runtime, console, and onboarding flows.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Friction heatmap documented and validated with 5 sales/solutions interviews and 3 customer sandbox tests. 2) Remediation backlog with owners and rough estimates (S,M,L). 3) Two prototypes deployed to staging (tokenizer adapter + quant-profile recommender) with demo runbook. 4) Test harness that runs model-swap smoke tests and generates pass/fail and quality delta metrics. 5) Exec one-pager approved by Head of Product.
notes: Avoid proposing changes that require breaking customer API contracts. Focus on compatibility layers, CLI migration helpers, and onboarding docs. Where possible prefer opt-in shims so hosted API users do not incur regression risk without consent.
